entries.title: Audiobook sales increased by 15% in September 2026
entries.summary: According to the Association of American Publishers, September 2026 total U.S. publishing revenue rose 9.5% year-over-year in September to about $1.5 billion. The post Audiobook sales increased by 15% in September 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Digital book revenues in the USA were down 2.5% to $83.5 million in September, while Digital Audiobook sales were up 15.1% to $105.3 million. Physical Audio revenues were up 25.1% to approximately $600 thousand. Year-to-date E-Book revenues were down 3.3% compared to 2025, totaling $768.7 million. Digital Audiobook revenue rose 12.9% to $911.6 million, while physical Audio revenue fell 7.7% to $4.1 million.

In terms of physical formats during the month of September, Hardback revenues were up 9.2%, coming in at $510.3 million; Paperbacks were up 15.0%, with $370.3 million in revenue; Mass Market was down 34.8% to $5.5 million; and Special Bindings were up 18.7%, with $35.0 million in revenue. Year-to-date Hardback revenues were up 4.3% to 7 billion; Mass Market was down 54.5% to $32.4 million; and Special Bindings were up 15.2% to $187.6 million.

Michael Kozlowski is the editor-in-chief at Good e-Reader and has written about audiobooks and e-readers for the past fifteen years. Newspapers and websites such as the CBC, CNET, Engadget, Huffington Post and the New York Times have picked up his articles. He Lives in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

entries.title: The Top 10 Best E-readers for 2026
entries.summary: The Good e-reader Top 10 List features the best e-readers to buy right now. We feature brands like Amazon, Kobo, PocketBook, Onyx, Remarkable, and more. The post The Top 10 Best E-readers for 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The top 10 e-readers of 2026 span black-and-white classics, color E Ink models, Android-powered devices, and large note-taking tablets from brands like Amazon, Kobo, and Onyx Boox. Good e-Reader releases our end-of-year top 10 recommendations now because no new devices will be released.

Many mainstream websites release their 2026 top lists in the first couple of months of the year, and they are out of date within six months. Publications guilty of this include Mashable, Engadget, Wired, and PCMag. Obviously, these are all general tech news sites and not specialized in e-readers like our website.

Amazon Kindle 2026

Amazon Kindle 16GB (newest model), Now thinner, lighter, and faster, 6" display, Ube

  • The redesigned Kindle: Now thinner, lighter, faster. New edge-to-edge color and a sleeker, 6" front display. Books open 30% faster vs. the previous Kindle.
  • Up to 6 weeks on a single charge: The display only uses power when you turn the page or use the front light.
  • Easy on the eyes: Read comfortably in bright sunlight or at night on a high-contrast, glare-free display with adjustable brightness.

The Amazon Kindle (2026) is a sleek, ultra-lightweight (140g) refresh of Amazon’s entry-level 6-inch e-reader, with a flush-front 300 PPI screen, faster page turns, a relocated side power button, and a user-replaceable battery to the base lineup. Available in a $149.99 plastic model (16GB, with ads) or a new $189.99 ad-free aluminum edition (32GB) in shades like Ube and Seaglass Green, it delivers crisp text and up to six weeks of battery life in a pocketable frame. However, critics note that the $40 price increase over its predecessor makes its ongoing omissions—no waterproofing, no warm front-light adjustment, and no physical page-turn buttons—harder to overlook when the 7-inch Paperwhite starts at just $199.99.

Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 2026

Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 16GB (newest model), Now thinner and lighter, 7" display, warm light...

  • The new Kindle Paperwhite: Thinner and lighter, with a high-contrast 7" display. New edge-to-edge color, fast page turns, and a waterproof design.
  • Up to 12 weeks on a single charge: The display only uses power when you turn the page or use the front light.
  • Built to last with a replaceable battery: If the time comes, the back panel opens for a quick battery swap. Snap it back into place and keep reading.

The Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2026) is an iterative, 13th-generation refresh of Amazon’s flagship 7-inch e-reader, with a slimmer 6.8mm profile, a relocated top-right power button, and a new user-replaceable battery designed to meet EU repairability rules. Retaining its crisp 300 PPI E Ink Carta 1300 screen with adjustable warm lighting, IPX8 waterproofing, and up to 12 weeks of battery life, it delivers noticeably faster page turns and deeper contrast, while the $249.99 Signature Edition adds an aluminum body, 32GB of storage, auto-adjusting brightness, and pogo-pin support for a new physical Page-Turn Cover. However, critics note that the base model’s $40 price hike to $199.99 still includes lock-screen ads unless you pay $20 more.

Pockebook Verta

Amazon Kindle 16GB (newest model), Now thinner, lighter, and faster, 6" display, Ube

  • The redesigned Kindle: Now thinner, lighter, faster. New edge-to-edge color and a sleeker, 6" front display. Books open 30% faster vs. the previous Kindle.
  • Up to 6 weeks on a single charge: The display only uses power when you turn the page or use the front light.
  • Easy on the eyes: Read comfortably in bright sunlight or at night on a high-contrast, glare-free display with adjustable brightness.

The PocketBook Verta is a newly released, ultra-lightweight (140g) 6-inch e-reader designed to succeed the Verse series, praised by early reviewers and outlets like The eBook Reader and TechRadar for its crisp 300 PPI E Ink Carta 1300 display, larger physical page-turn buttons, and customizable, swappable back panels. Priced at $169 USD (with a color Kaleido 3 variant at $179.99), it features a faster quad-core processor with 1GB of RAM, warm SMARTlight illumination, Bluetooth audiobook support, native Libby integration, and broad compatibility with 25 file formats without locking users into a closed ecosystem. However, its water resistance is downgraded from the Verse Pro’s full submersion rating to basic IPX4 splash protection; it lacks an external microSD card slot, and its Linux-based interface can still feel slightly sluggish compared to Kindle or Kobo rivals despite the upgraded hardware.

reMarkable Paper Pure

reMarkable Paper Pure Digital Notebook with Marker Plus | 10.3” paper tablet with black and white...

  • The new reMarkable Paper Pure: Close the gap between how you think and work. This paper tablet combines the proven benefits of handwriting with software that simplifies everyday work tasks, like getting your thoughts down on paper, reviewing documents, and staying focused in meetings.
  • Our best black-and-white paper tablet yet: The third-generation 10.3-inch display is whiter and has more contrast than ever before. Digital ink appears in just 21 ms — faster than the blink of an eye.
  • Your place to think: Just put your pen to paper and take notes, mark up documents, and sketch. With dozens of available note-taking templates, an uncluttered screen, and easy navigation, thoughts can flow without interruption.

The reMarkable Paper Pure is an entry-level, 10.3-inch monochrome E Ink writing tablet with an ultra-lightweight recycled-plastic build, multi-week battery life, and responsive, pencil-like writing feel using the active Marker stylus. Replacing the aging reMarkable 2 at a $399 USD starting price (around $549.99–$629 CAD), it delivers the company’s signature distraction-free OS with no apps or notifications, alongside a repair-friendly design. However, critics at Engadget note several deliberate compromises to hit its lower price point—including the lack of a front light for reading in dim rooms, a lower 226 PPI resolution, no support for physical keyboard accessories, and ongoing reliance on a Connect subscription for full cloud and software features.

Durobo Krono

Durobo Krono – 6.13" Smart Digital Paper Focus Hub, 300 PPI 6G 128G Paper Tablet, with Smart Dial...

  • Thoughts Rest, Ideas Bloom- Step away from distractions and into clarity. With its paper-like screen and compact form, Krono offers a space to nurture new ideas, where every pause becomes the start of something meaningful.
  • ​Embracing minimalist aesthetics, Krono exudes calm geometric beauty, a nod to traditional mechanical design. Compact and portable, Krono easily fits in your hand or pocket, keeping you company on commutes, workouts, or trips.
  • Feel Natural on the Eyes- 300 PPI. Krono features an E Ink HD display, delivering a pure paper-like aesthetic. You can see the delicate texture unique to paper. Millions of tiny microcapsules filled with black particles render sharp, crisp text, with each letter edge clean and refined.

The DuRoBo Krono is a pocket-sized, smartphone-style Android 15 e-reader and distraction-free “focus hub” and has a crisp 6.13-inch E Ink Carta 1200 display, snappy octa-core performance, and full Google Play Store support for apps like Kindle, Libby, and Audible. While its 3,950 mAh battery easily lasts over a week and its built-in Spark AI voice-memo transcription is handy for quick notes, critics note that the physical side scroll wheel feels loose, customization is limited, and the device lacks both a microSD card slot and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Ultimately, it is a compelling, ultra-portable e-reader for people who want multi-app flexibility without phone notifications.

Xteink X4 Pro

XTEINK X4 Pro 4.3 Inch eBook Reader with Front Light & Touchscreen,Magnetic | 4.3" E-Book reader...

  • Ultra-Compact, Magnetic & Portable: Exceptionally compact with a 5.95mm ultra-thin profile and 72g (2.5 oz) lightweight design. Fits effortlessly into any pocket or palm, featuring a built-in magnetic back for seamless attachment and portable carry anywhere.
  • Eye-Care E-Ink with Dual-Tone Front Light: Premium 4.3" paper-feel display that eliminates screen glare and eye fatigue. Equipped with multi-level warm and cool front light controls for a comfortable reading experience in bright sunlight or complete darkness.
  • Touchscreen & Physical Page-Turn Buttons: Features intuitive single-point touch and gesture swiping combined with tactile side page-turn buttons. Offers dual control options for fluid, precise, and effort-free page navigation.

The XTEINK X4 Pro is a highly portable, 4.3-inch pocket e-reader designed as a distraction-free alternative to smartphone doomscrolling. Reviewers from platforms like WIRED praise its featherlight 72-gram body and major hardware upgrades over previous iterations, most notably the addition of a responsive touchscreen and an integrated dual-tone front light with adjustable color temperatures for nighttime reading. To support these power-hungry additions, the manufacturer nearly doubled the battery capacity to 1,100 mAh while maintaining an ultra-thin 5.95 mm profile with built-in magnets for easy phone attachment. This device costs $99 on their website.

Kobo Clara BW

Kobo Clara BW | eReader | 6” Glare-Free Touchscreen with ComfortLight PRO | Dark Mode Option...

  • 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗬 𝗔𝗡𝗬 𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘 - Glare-free 6” E Ink Carta 1300 HD lets you read in bright sunlight without reflections with fast page-turns and optional Dark Mode for better nighttime reading
  • 𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗬 𝗢𝗡 𝗬𝗢𝗨𝗥 𝗘𝗬𝗘𝗦 - Use ComfortLight PRO to adjust your eReader’s brightness, colour temperature, and blue light so you won’t be kept awake
  • 𝗜𝗣𝗫𝟴 𝗪𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗢𝗙 𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗𝗘𝗥 – Full waterproof protection and meets requirements of IPX8 rating – waterproof for up to 60 minutes in up to 2 metres of water

The Kobo Clara BW is a compact, ultra-lightweight (174g) 6-inch e-reader with a crisp 300 PPI E Ink Carta 1300 screen, ComfortLight PRO adjustable warm lighting, IPX8 waterproofing, and iFixit-backed self-repairability—in an affordable, ad-free package. Equipped with 16GB of storage, native OverDrive/Libby library borrowing, broad EPUB sideloading support, and Bluetooth audiobook playback, it offers superior text contrast and responsiveness over E Ink rivals. However, Good e-Reader notes that its recessed screen and basic recycled-plastic casing feel utilitarian; it lacks physical page-turn buttons, microSD expansion, and native Dropbox or Google Drive integration, unless you pay for the new Kobo Stack.

Onyx Boox Palma 3

BOOX Palma 3 ePaper Reader 6.13 inch B/W 6GB + 128GB with Front Light | 300PPI, Matte and...

  • Screen: 6.13" HD Carta1300 glass screen with flat cover-lens Resolution: B/W: 824 x 1648 (300ppi)
  • OS: Android 16 Document Formats: PDF (reflowable), EPUB, Adobe DRM, TXT, RTF, HTML, CHM, DOC, FB2. Image Formats: PNG, JPG, BMP, TIFF. Audio Formats: WAV, MP3 Supports 3rd-party apps
  • Button: Power Button with Fingerprint Recognition, Volume/Page-Turn Buttons, Customizable Function Button USB-C Port (Supports OTG or use as an audio jack) Battery: 3,950mAh Li-ion Polymer Dimensions: 159 x 78 x 7.8 mm (6.3"" x 3.1"" x 0.3"") Weight: Approx. 195 g (6.2 oz)

The Onyx Boox Palma 3 is a smartphone-sized, monochrome Android 16 e-reader with a sharp 6.13-inch, 300 PPI E Ink display, a noticeably faster 4nm octa-core processor, and a refined anodized aluminum frame with a paper-textured backplate. Priced at $319.99 USD, it packs 6GB of RAM, 128GB of storage with microSD expansion up to 2TB, physical page-turn and programmable smart buttons, a fingerprint power sensor, and full Google Play Store access—plus new active stylus support via the optional InkSense Plus pen for quick pocket note-taking. However, critics note that the metal build makes it slightly heavier than earlier plastic models, there is no built-in loop or magnetic attachment for storing the stylus, and the narrow screen makes extended handwriting cramped—while the lack of color and 4G cellular data makes it more of a sidegrade for existing Palma 2 Pro owners.

Amazon Kindle Colorsosft 2026

Amazon Kindle Colorsoft 16GB (newest model), Now thinner and lighter, 7" color display, warm light...

  • The new Kindle Colorsoft: Thinner and lighter, with a 7" paper-like color display. New edge-to-edge color, waterproof design, no ads.
  • Color your pages: Paper-like color perfect for comics, graphic novels, and more. Highlight your favorite scenes in yellow, orange, blue, pink, and green.
  • Up to 8 weeks on a single charge: The display only uses power when you turn the page or use the front light.

The Amazon Kindle Colorsoft (2026) is a sleek, second-generation hardware refresh of Amazon’s 7-inch color e-reader, praised for its thinner 6.8mm chassis, relocated side power button, user-replaceable battery, and more uniform frontlight that resolves the first generation’s yellow-band display issues. Available in a $289.99 plastic standard model (16GB) or a $319.99 aluminum Signature Edition (32GB) in Graphite or Fig—both ad-free by default with IPX8 waterproofing and pogo-pin support for the new Page-Turn Cover—it delivers fast page turns, multi-color highlighting, and seamless Kindle store integration. However, because it retains the same Kaleido 3 color filter layer (300 PPI monochrome / 150 PPI color), its unlit screen remains noticeably darker than the monochrome Paperwhite, requiring higher frontlight levels that cut into battery life, while the removal of Qi wireless charging and the steep price make it a tough sell unless you regularly read comics, illustrated books, or color annotations inside Amazon’s ecosystem.

Boox Picco

BOOX Picco 3.97" (235ppi) B/W eReader with Front Light & Touchscreen USB-C Charging Pocket eBook...

  • Screen: 3.97" with an anti-glare (AG) glass cover and narrow bezels Resolution: 800 x 480(235ppi) Front Light: 2800-6300k
  • Dimensions: 105.5 x 62 x 5.5 mm (4.15" x 2.44" x 0.22") Weight: Approx. 58g (2.04 oz) Battery: 920mAh
  • Flash:16 MB built-in Flash plus an external TF card slot supporting up to 2 TB (exFAT, with FAT32 support) Connector: USB-C, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth BLE.

The Onyx Boox Picco is an ultra-portable, 3.97-inch E-Ink pocket reader priced around $110 that excels at distraction-free reading on the go, featuring a slim aluminum build, customizable physical page-turn buttons, a dual-tone front light, and a microSD slot. Unlike standard Boox tablets, it does not run Android or support third-party app stores, instead offering a streamlined interface with basic extras like a Pomodoro timer, to-do list, and reading stats while transferring books via USB-C, microSD, or a companion app. Reviewers praise its pocketability, optional magnetic case for snapping onto phones, and clean UI, though its tiny screen and lack of DRM support limit it mostly to DRM-free EPUBs or public domain books as a secondary reader rather than a primary one.

entries.title: Supernote releases LAMY Safari Vista and AL-star EMR Pen Plus
entries.summary: Supernote has announced that the Supernote × LAMY Safari Vista EMR Pen Plus will ship in December, and that the Supernote × LAMY AL-star EMR Pen Plus is available now. The post Supernote releases LAMY Safari Vista and AL-star EMR Pen Plus first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Supernote has just announced two new EMR styluses that have been designed by Lamy. The Supernote × LAMY Safari Vista EMR Pen Plus is an upgraded version of Supernote’s transparent LAMY stylus. It combines Supernote’s ceramic nib with a customizable side button for the first time in the Vista lineup and ships out in December for $119.99.

The Supernote × LAMY AL-star EMR Pen Plus is the metal-bodied sibling to the Safari Vista EMR Pen Plus. Co-engineered by Supernote and LAMY, it pairs a black anodized aluminum body with Supernote’s 0.65 mm Ceramic NeverReplace Nib and a customizable side button. This pen is available in very limited quantities and retails for $119.00.

Early impressions and reviews of the Supernote × LAMY safari vista EMR Pen Plus highlight it as a long-requested upgrade that finally pairs Supernote’s permanent ceramic nib with a functional side button. Reviewers and users on Reddit praise the refined 0.65 mm nib for noticeably sharper, cleaner detail in small handwriting, alongside the internal drop-protection spring and lightweight (20 g) transparent body that reduces hand fatigue during long writing sessions. However, common criticisms include its steep price tag, a molded triangular grip that can feel uncomfortable if you don’t hold your pen with a standard tripod grip, and the fact that on newer Manta and Nomad tablets, the side button is restricted to a single shortcut (either eraser or lasso) rather than switching functions based on hover distance.

The Supernote × LAMY AL-star EMR Pen Plus is praised for its matte black anodized aluminum body, which offers a well-balanced, substantial feel (22 g) that comes close to rivaling the Heart of Metal series while adding the long-awaited combination of a 0.65 mm ceramic nib and a customizable side button. Reviewers note that the finer ceramic nib delivers crisp precision for small handwriting and benefits from an internal spring for drop protection, while the side button makes one-handed erasing or lassoing far more reliable than two-finger screen gestures. On the downside, some YouTube testers mention a short learning curve to avoid accidentally pressing the flush side button, depending on your grip. However, it is limited to a black-only color option, and newer Manta and Nomad tablets lock the button to a single mapped function rather than supporting distance-based dual shortcuts.

entries.title: Pocketbook InkPad Eo 2 Review
entries.summary: Featuring a large, eye-safe 10.3-inch color display and handwriting recognition tools, PocketBook Stylus 2 is built for professionals, students, creators, and everyday note-takers alike. The post Pocketbook InkPad Eo 2 Review first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 is a newly released 10.3-inch color E Ink note-taking tablet running Android 14, priced lower than the original InkPad Eo by dropping the camera and switching to an in-house active stylus. Because full long-term reviews are still emerging after its late-2026 release, early hands-on impressions highlight clear hardware trade-offs worth weighing before buying.

The PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 is a 10.3-inch color e-note tablet that features an E Ink Kaleido 3 display, offering a sharp 300 DPI for grayscale content (1860 x 2480) and 150 DPI for its 4,096-color mode (930 x 1240). Running on an open Android 14 operating system with full access to the Google Play Store, the device is powered by an octa-core MediaTek MT6765 processor clocked at 2.3GHz, paired with 4GB of RAM and 64GB of internal storage, which can be expanded via a microSD slot. To ensure visibility in any environment, it incorporates a SMARTlight frontlight system that lets users adjust both screen brightness and color temperature.

Underneath the hood is one of the fastest processors PocketBook has ever employed in a device. The octa-core 2.3GHZ processor will ensure all your programs and apps launch at lightning speed. There is 4GB of RAM and 64GB of internal storage; there is also an SD card. There is a G-sensor, dual-band WIFI, and Bluetooth 5.0 for listening to audiobooks or music; if you don’t feel like using headphones, there are dual stereo speakers. There are four microphones, which are suitable for voice communication apps. A USB-C port transfers data from your PC or MAC to the device and charges. It is powered by a 4000 mAh battery, has 191x226x7mm dimensions, and weighs 470g.

Unlike the first-generation model, which supports the WACOM stylus, this model uses a proprietary active digital stylus (the PocketBook Stylus 2) for AI-powered handwriting recognition. The Pen needs to be recharged. Physically, the device measures 191 x 225.6 x 7 mm, houses a USB-C port for charging and data transfer, and showcases a distinct, premium pinstriped backplate design.

Handwriting remains one of the fastest and most natural ways to capture ideas. With a built-in AI recognition feature, InkPad Eo 2 instantly converts handwritten notes into clear, editable text, eliminating the need for manual transcription. Whether documenting meeting outcomes, organizing lecture notes, preparing reports, or developing creative concepts, users can quickly transform handwritten content into digital files ready for editing, sharing, and archiving. Supporting over 40 languages, this handwriting recognition tool helps make note-taking faster, smarter, and more versatile.

The InkPad Eo 2 brings a newer Android version and a lower price tag than the first-generation model, making it appealing if you want a large color E Ink screen with Play Store apps on a tighter budget. However, buyers who want a built-in camera, Wacom stylus compatibility, or proven long-term software polish should buy the InkPad Eo 1.

entries.title: Pocketbook InkPad EO vs the Pocketbook InkPad Eo 2
entries.summary: Both models share the exact same MediaTek MT6765 chip, 4 GB of RAM, stereo speakers, four-microphone array, and 470 g mist-grey aluminum body. Even the Eo 2's AI handwriting recognition tools are rolling out to the original Eo via firmware updates The post Pocketbook InkPad EO vs the Pocketbook InkPad Eo 2 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
While the Eo 2 is numbered as a sequel, it is actually a cost-reduced hardware revision with an updated OS, not a complete spec overhaul. Both devices share the exact same 10.3-inch color E Ink screen, processor, RAM, storage, and chassis. I would choose the PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 for its modern Android 14 operating system and lower price point, unless a Wacom stylus and document-scanning camera are strict must-haves for your workflow.

Between the two, the PocketBook InkPad Eo 2 is the smarter buy for most people because of its updated Android 14 software, larger battery, and lower price, even though it drops a few hardware extras. Both devices share the exact same 10.3-inch Kaleido 3 color E Ink display, octa-core processor, 4 GB of RAM, and 64 GB of expandable storage, meaning reading and general navigation feel identical. However, the original Eo launched with an aging Android 11 operating system that limits long-term app compatibility, whereas the Eo 2 jumps to Android 14 and bumps the battery capacity from 4,000 mAh to 4,900 mAh for noticeably better endurance.

The trade-off for the Eo 2’s lower retail price and modern software is the loss of its Wacom stylus layer and rear camera. On the original Eo, you get an 8 MP rear camera for scanning physical documents to mark up, alongside a battery-free Wacom EMR pen with a built-in eraser that works with popular third-party styluses. To cut costs on the Eo 2, PocketBook removed the camera entirely and switched to an active capacitive pen (the Stylus 2) that lacks a rear eraser, blocks third-party Wacom pens, and requires periodic USB-C charging—a worthwhile compromise unless heavy, Wacom-specific sketching is your top priority.

entries.title: Audible is launching a new royalty model for publishers
entries.summary: By year-end, the legacy royalty model will be discontinued, and rights holders will need to enroll their titles in the new model to continue distribution with Audible. The post Audible is launching a new royalty model for publishers first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Audible is transitioning all rights holders to a pooled, engagement-based royalty model by December 31, 2026, replacing its legacy per-sale system. Rights holders who do not sign the updated contract amendments by the end-of-year deadline will have their titles removed from distribution on the platform.

On paper, the new publishing rates look appealing: Audible Creation Exchange creators will see their royalty percentages jump from 40% to 50% for exclusive titles and from 25% to 30% for non-exclusive ones, alongside new options to suggest list prices and opt non-exclusive books into the All-You-Can-Listen (Audible Plus) catalog. However, rather than paying a straightforward cut of a book’s retail or credit value, Audible now takes a subscriber’s total monthly membership value and divides it proportionally across every audiobook that user listens to in a given month, weighted by engagement and à la carte price.

Direct cash purchases from non-members or members buying outside their credits still pay a direct percentage at the higher 50% or 30% rates. Creators can also now submit a suggested retail price for their titles, though Audible retains final pricing control.

In practice, the model is a major mixed bag that has drawn sharp criticism from independent authors and narrators. While creators with backlist titles or high-completion listens in the All-You-Can-Listen tier can benefit from steady streaming payouts, authors relying on traditional credit sales often face “pool dilution.” If a listener uses a monthly credit on your book but also streams several Audible Plus titles that same month, a slice of that subscriber’s membership fee is diverted to those streams—meaning your actual dollar payout can shrink despite the higher percentage rate. Ultimately, it shifts Audible closer to a Spotify-style streaming economy, rewarding listener retention while making per-sale earnings far less predictable.

Any indie authors and narrators have raised concerns that splitting a single member’s monthly value across multiple engaged titles—including AYCL listening—can make monthly payouts less predictable or dilute earnings from credit purchases compared to the legacy model. Opinions are mixed: some worry credit-purchased titles effectively subsidize AYCL listening, while others suggest exploring alternatives like Spotify or Libro.fm.

Wrap up

This new royalty change will not affect the broader Audible experience for listeners who subscribe to Audible Standard and Audible Premium. The mainstream audiobooks, podcasts, and original content will stay the same. Publishers and indie authors will certainly not love the new pooling system; instead of being paid for each title a consumer listens to, they have no choice. Audible is the largest audiobook site in the world, and Spotify Audiobooks or Libbo.fm do not come close.

Audible holds an estimated 60% to 65% of the U.S. audiobook revenue market, with similar dominance across the UK, Canada, and Australia. Because Amazon does not break out Audible’s standalone financials—and the Audio Publishers Association (APA) reports aggregate industry sales rather than platform-level splits—analysts anchor 2026 platform estimates to the 63.4% revenue share benchmark.

Michael Kozlowski is the editor-in-chief at Good e-Reader and has written about audiobooks and e-readers for the past fifteen years. entries.title: XTEINK Black Friday: Finding the Best Pocket E-Reader Gift
entries.summary: A pocket e-reader doesn't need to be attached to a phone to display a book. XTEINK's magnetic backs can be used with compatible accessories, but each model works as an independent reader The post XTEINK Black Friday: Finding the Best Pocket E-Reader Gift first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Buying an e-reader for someone who loves books sounds simple until you consider how they read. A novel beside the bed, ebooks on a laptop, or a lamp left on late can reveal more than a specification sheet. XTEINK’s X3, X4 Classic, and X4 Pro offer three variations on a compact E Ink reader, with differences that matter long after the wrapping paper is gone.

Start with the books, not the device

An existing ebook collection is often the most useful clue. Someone who downloads EPUB novels may find it easy to move compatible files to a new reader. Someone whose purchases are tied to a particular bookstore app might have a harder time. The XTEINK models support compatible EPUB and TXT files, but ebooks protected by incompatible digital rights management (DRM) will not necessarily transfer.

Check this before choosing a gift, perhaps by asking where the recipient buys books. A new reader is more enjoyable when its owner already has something to read. You could also include a handwritten note recommending a book they might enjoy, rather than guessing which titles they would want preloaded.

The appeal of a truly small screen

The X3 is a mini e-reader with a 3.7-inch E Ink display, weighing just 58 grams. It has physical controls and no built-in front light. Its 259 PPI screen can show fine lettering, although the available reading area is still small.

That distinction matters more than the numbers suggest. A reflowable novel can adapt to the narrow display, but larger type means fewer words on each page. Someone reading fiction a few pages at a time may enjoy that format. A person who spends hours with detailed charts or scanned academic material is likely to find a screen this small restrictive. The X3 is easier to recommend when you know what the recipient likes to read.

A little more page, without touch controls

The X4 Classic gives text more room with a 4.3-inch screen, while keeping its weight at 68 grams. Page-turn buttons sit on both sides of the frame, and motion-based page turning is available too. There is no touchscreen, so readers use physical controls to navigate the device as well as to turn pages.

That might suit someone who enjoys the feel of a button under their thumb. It also means moving through menus can take more steps than a quick tap. These are small differences that become noticeable in regular use.

The Classic has no front light, either. A recipient who normally reads with a desk lamp may be perfectly comfortable with that arrangement. Someone who likes reading in a dark bedroom will need an additional light source.

For the book that stays open after dark

The X4 Pro keeps the 4.3-inch screen and physical page-turn buttons but adds a touchscreen and adjustable front lighting with warm and cool settings. Finding a title or changing an option is more direct with touch navigation. When the room gets dim, the light can be adjusted without switching on a bedside lamp.

At 72 grams, the Pro is only slightly heavier than the Classic. It also supports XTEINK’s Ink Apps, including a clock and a to-do list. Those extras are not essential to reading, but they may be welcome to someone who likes keeping a few simple tools on an E Ink screen. The Pro may suit a recipient who reads at different times of day, although its small screen still limits complex documents.

A gift that is ready to be used

A pocket e-reader doesn’t need to be attached to a phone to display a book. XTEINK’s magnetic backs can be used with compatible accessories, but each model works as an independent reader.

Before wrapping it, consider what the recipient will need on the first day: a compatible book, a suitable lamp if the model has no front light, and a little guidance on transferring files. A little preparation makes the gift easier to enjoy.

The Black Friday prices

For Black Friday 2026, XTEINK lists the X3 at $55, the X4 Classic at $59, and the X4 Pro at $99.

An additional 10% discount is available to the first 1,000 eligible customers purchasing an X4 Pro together with either an X3 or an X4 Classic. That brings the X4 Pro + X3 total to $138.60 and the X4 Pro + X4 Classic total to $142.20. The X3 + X4 Classic pairing does not qualify for this discount.

The two-reader offers may be useful when choosing gifts for two people with different reading habits. Individual models are also available. Specifications and final checkout conditions can be checked on the official XTEINK X3, X4 Classic, and X4 Pro product pages.

Markus lives in San Francisco, California and is the video game and audio expert on Good e-Reader! He has a huge interest in new e-readers and tablets, and gaming.

entries.title: Aura Ink 10-inch Spectra 6 e-paper frame is available now
entries.summary: The Aura Ink 10" is a compact, cordless 10-inch color E Ink digital photo frame designed to look like a traditional framed print without a glowing screen or power cable. The post Aura Ink 10-inch Spectra 6 e-paper frame is available now first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Earlier this month, Aura, the leading innovator in smart photo frames, launched E INK Spectra 6 with the new nine-color E INK panel. This photo frame. Instead of the intense, random full-screen flashing on the 13-inch original, the Ink 10 updates overnight using a gentler, wave-like ripple pattern. It is available now and retails for $349 from their website.

The Aura Ink 10 delivers the cord-free, print-like e-paper experience in a smaller frame designed for more versatility across the home, from desks and shelves to side tables and gallery walls. The frame moves to the new Spectra 6 paper panel with a nine-color e-paper display—expanding the palette from six to nine by adding off-white, mustard yellow, and orange—alongside a 200 PPI display, the highest pixel density Aura has brought to e-paper. The result is sharper detail, richer skin tones, and smoother color transitions, especially in the family photos Aura customers display most.

Aura’s proprietary dithering algorithm, refined specifically around family photography, calculates each pixel in relation to those surrounding it to produce the appearance of millions of tones from a physically limited ink palette. Like Ink 13″, the frame features an adaptive frontlight that automatically adjusts to the room’s ambient light — adding contrast and gentle vibrancy without turning the frame into another glowing screen — and runs for up to three months on a single charge. Ink 10″ is also Calm Tech Certified Platinum, the highest designation from the Calm Tech Institute.

Key Points

  • Nine-color e-paper display: Aura worked closely with E Ink to expand the palette from six to nine, adding off-white, mustard yellow, and orange — creating more even colors on faces, richer detail in textures like grass, and more natural transitions in gradients like a sky at sunset.
  • 200 PPI resolution: Higher pixel density in a smaller footprint means sharper, more detailed photos.
  • Proprietary dithering algorithm: Aura continued refining its proprietary dithering algorithm specifically around family photography. By calculating each pixel in relation to those surrounding it, Ink 10″ creates the appearance of millions of tones and more nuanced color transitions from a limited physical ink palette.
  • Cordless by nature: Up to three months of battery life on a single charge, allowing photos to live anywhere a plugged-in frame can’t.

    Adaptive lighting: Subtle, art-like front light automatically adjusts to ambient conditions, adding vibrancy without a distracting glow. For more control, users can schedule the light to turn on and off at specific times each day.
  • Overnight Refresh: Refreshes overnight to show a new photo each day, though you can see more images using the app or on-frame buttons. Ink 10″ also comes with a new transition for anyone who chooses a more frequent photo refresh for their frame. Overnight updates still use a longer flashing refresh to help prevent burn-in.
  • Calm Tech Certified Platinum: The highest recognition from the Calm Tech Institute, reserved for products that meet its strictest standards for technology designed around human well-being.
  • Effortless setup and unlimited sharing: Like all Aura frames, Ink 10″ connects through the Aura Frames app, with free unlimited photo storage and no subscription required. Invite contributors to share memories from anywhere.

entries.title: Kodak SlideTag is a color E INK Keychain
entries.summary: Kodak SlideTag is a retro keychain accessory featuring a 1.54-inch, 6-color E Ink panel with a 240 × 240-pixel resolution, compatible with Android and iOS. The post Kodak SlideTag is a color E INK Keychain first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Kodak SlideTag is a retro-inspired keychain accessory made by Kodak licensee Reto that combines a miniature color E Ink digital photo frame with a Bluetooth item tracker. Styled after classic 1935 Kodachrome 35mm slide mounts, it launched on November 22, 2026.

The Kodak SlideTag earns strong early praise from reviewers for blending retro nostalgia with genuine everyday utility, standing out as a major step up in build quality and durability compared to Reto’s earlier novelty gadgets. Styled after a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount, it features a 1.54-inch, 6-color E Ink screen with a 240 x 240 resolution and delivers a charming, lo-fi aesthetic that draws zero power when displaying static images.

Beyond cycling through up to 12 uploaded photos via the free Kodak Memory Link app, the display doubles as a surprisingly practical tool for showing QR codes, contact details, calendars, countdowns, or short to-do lists. Compatibility with both Apple Find My and Google Find Hub, plus an IP54 splash-resistance rating and a user-replaceable lithium coin-cell battery, makes it a genuinely useful keychain companion rather than disposable shelf decor. It also supports Bluetooth 5.4 for maximum compatibility.

entries.title: Amazon Alexa Tablets on sale for Black Friday
entries.summary: Amazon's all-new 2026 Alexa Tablet lineup—which replaced the older Fire tablets with full Android and Google Play Store support—is heavily discounted for Black Friday The post Amazon Alexa Tablets on sale for Black Friday first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon’s all-new 2026 Alexa Tablet lineup—which replaced the older Fire tablets with full Android and Google Play Store support—is heavily discounted for Black Friday across Amazon’s websites and all of its retail partners. The savings are huge, up to 43% off the list price.

Reviewers largely agree that Amazon’s 2026 Alexa Tablet lineup is a major step forward from the old Fire tablets, primarily because it replaces the restrictive Fire OS with full Android 16 and native Google Play Store access. Publications like CNN Underscored and TechRadar praise the upgraded aluminum unibody designs across all three models (8, 11, and 12 Pro), noting that they look and feel much closer to modern iPads than plastic budget slates. Critics highlight the 12 Pro’s optional anti-glare Nanomatte 120Hz display and distraction-free Kindle reading modes as standout features for e-books, comics, and note-taking, while some readers point out that Amazon’s promise of seven years of OS and security updates adds strong long-term value.

Kindle Mode is a built-in reading profile on Amazon’s 2026 Alexa Tablets (8, 11, and 12 Pro) that automatically transforms the display and system behavior whenever you open a book in the native Kindle app. Once you close your book or exit the app, the tablet immediately reverts to its normal Android 16 interface and standard color settings.

However, reviewers note several trade-offs that hold the lineup back from beating rivals like the base iPad or mid-range Galaxy Tabs. 9to5Google reports noticeable UI stuttering and modest MediaTek performance on the entry-level Alexa Tablet 8 and 11, alongside flat speakers, basic cameras, and the removal of microSD card slots and headphone jacks. Additionally, base models still ship with lockscreen ads unless you pay extra to remove them, and testers found the built-in Alexa+ assistant inconsistent for everyday tasks—making these tablets best suited for media consumption, reading, and casual browsing—especially when heavily discounted—rather than heavy gaming or pro-level work.
